newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT - Cocoa signs seen bullish for medium-term.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Cocoa signs seen bullish for medium-term.

text.p: JULY Close * Support * Resist * RSI14 * MA10 * MA30
LIFFE cocoa futures have turned technically bullish after Thursday's convincing breakout to contract highs amid the heaviest daily turnover since March 31, 1995, analysts said.
July cocoa was called to open 10 stg per tonne higher on Friday after closing strongly at 1,076, just off its contract high of 1,088.
"Support is a long way away now from the closing price," said independent technical analyst Elli Gifford.
She said initial September support rested at Thursday's low of 1,059. Further support was seen at the bottom of a chart gap left from Wednesday's high of 1,046 and Thursday's low of 1,025.
"But I don't think the gap will get filled," Gifford said. "If it does get filled, I would get nervous about cocoa's outlook."

Instead, Gifford expected cocoa to retrace in the very near term some of Thursday's whopping gains, test initial support and fail to fall through. Once support held, she expected cocoa to resume its strong rally.
In the intermediate term, Gifford was looking for September to move to 1,142. If that broke, she saw a move up to 1,165.
Longer-term, if September cleared those initial hurdles, she predicted a "bull market in cocoa that we haven't seen in quite a while" that could power September up to 1,300.
She said all technical signals were flashing buy signals, though monthly charts were not yet as strong as the near- and intermediate-signals.
